_____________________________________________________ HON'BLE MRS.
JUSTICE SABINA Judgment 23/01/2018 Petitioner had faced trial under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act').
Trial Court vide judgment/order dated 02.04.2002 ordered the conviction and sentence of the petitioner under Section 7/16 of the Act.
Appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed by the Appellate Court vide order dated 23.07.2004.
Hence, the present petition by the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that as per the prosecution case petitioner was found in possession of adulterated milk.
Occurrence in the present case is of the year 1991.
Petitioner is facing criminal proceedings since the year 1991.

Learned counsel has submitted that he does not challenge the conviction of the petitioner as ordered by the courts below but has submitted that the sentence of the petitioner qua (2 of 2) [CRLR-726/2004] imprisonment be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
Petitioner is not a previous convict and is the sole bread earner of his family.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of this court in Loonaram Vs. The State of Rajasthan WLN (UC) 1977, 571 and on the judgments of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Bharat Lal Vs. The State of Haryana 1993(2) FAC Cases 65, Mahabir Parashad Vs. The State of Haryana 1993(2) FAC Cases 83 and Anil Kumar Vs.
State of Haryana 2015(2) FAC 381.

sentences.text: Learned State Counsel has opposed the petition.
Keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and expedient to reduce the sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner to the period period already undergone by him.
Accordingly, conviction of the petitioner under Section 7/16 of the Act is maintained.

However,
sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner is reduced to the period already undergone by him and petitioner is directed to deposit the additional fine to the tune of Rs. 10,000/- before the trial Court.

Petitioner is granted two months time from today to deposit the amount of additional fine, failing Ranjeet vs State on 23 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193124444/
1 which this petition shall be deemed to have been dismissed.
Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
(SABINA)J. Sudha/05 Ranjeet vs State on 23 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193124444/
